text:
**For most buyers, LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice.** Nearly every current power station uses it, and the sources agree on the main reasons.

**Where LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** Rated LFP stations typically claim 3,000-4,000+ cycles, versus roughly 500-800 for the NMC models. That is about 8-11 years of daily cycling versus 1.5-2 years ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). One site puts NMC at 1,000-2,000 cycles ([PowerStationMatch](https://powerstationmatch.com/learn/lifepo4-vs-nmc)), so claims vary by model.
- **Failure behavior:** In lab tests, LFP cells burned cooler and less violently than NMC cells (peaks around 259°C versus 731°C in one study). That matters if you keep the unit indoors or in a vehicle ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- **Price:** The NMC discount has largely disappeared. One retailer guide lists a median of about $0.55/Wh for LFP versus $0.95/Wh for NMC, and LFP costs far less per rated cycle ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

**Where NMC wins**
- **Energy density:** NMC cells hold more energy per pound. In finished stations the gap is small, about 10-16% by median, and some LFP models are lighter per Wh than some NMC ones. Compare the actual specs of the models you're considering.

**Caveats**
- LFP is not fireproof. It can still fail, and it reached thermal runaway sooner in one overcharge test ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). Some sites overstate its safety.
- Cold weather depends more on the maker than on the chemistry. Most stations of both types won't charge below 32°F, so check the manual.
- Cycle ratings aren't directly comparable. Some are rated to 70% capacity and others to 80%, and test conditions differ. Look for the end point (for example, "3,000 cycles to 80%").

**When NMC can still make sense**
- You use it only a few times a year and found a deeply discounted unit.
- Weight is critical, and you've checked that the specific NMC model is actually lighter.
- You already own a working NMC unit, in which case keep using it.

**Choosing a model**
Pick by capacity and output first, and chemistry second. A long-lived battery doesn't help if the inverter can't start your fridge. Check the spec sheet for "LiFePO4" or "LFP," the cycle rating with its end point, and the warranty length.

The sources named a few LFP examples: the [Anker SOLIX C1000](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/) (1,056 Wh, 3,000 cycles to 80%, 5-year warranty) and the [EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/) (286 Wh). I don't have retailer or checkout links for them in these results, so those links go to the guide that lists their specs. They are examples, not recommendations.
